title: OpenAI told by 15 attorney general to preserve Hugging Face evidence
excerpt: They wrote in a letter that OpenAI is either unable or unwilling to ensure the safety of its products, posing a risk of substantial harm to Americans.
content_html:
15 attorneys general have instructed OpenAI to preserve all materials related to the Hugging Face hack

By Aditi Bharade

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

OpenAI is facing intense legal scrutiny over the July hacking incident on Hugging Face.

In a letter to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman on Monday, the attorneys general of 15 states wrote that the Hugging Face hack showed that OpenAI is unable or unwilling to ensure the safety of its products. They said this "poses an imminent risk of substantial harm" to Americans, and demanded that the company preserve relevant evidence.

On July 21, OpenAI said its GPT-5.6 Sol model had escaped its sandbox during a cybersecurity challenge and accessed Hugging Face's internal databases.

The attorneys general wrote that the AI lab had "failed to confirm that its secure and isolated testing environment was, in fact, secure and isolated," despite the "severe risks posed by the scenario."

They flagged one particular red flag from the hacking, citing a July 24 Reuters exclusive that said OpenAI's agent "left notes apparently for future versions of itself" on how to break free from OpenAI's restraints.

"OpenAI's unprecedented and alarming misconduct demands an immediate and significant response," the group wrote, adding that the company may have violated state and federal law, including consumer protection and data privacy statutes.

They instructed OpenAI to immediately preserve all materials related to the Hugging Face hacking incident, as well as any prior instances in which its agents similarly engaged in unauthorized intrusions into computer systems or databases.

The letter was signed by the attorneys general of Iowa, Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Idaho, Indiana, Kansas, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Texas, and Utah.

In response to a request for comment from Business Insider, an OpenAI spokesperson said: "This incident marks an important moment for AI safety and we take the questions raised by the Attorneys General seriously."

The spokesperson said that the company is conducting a thorough review with external advisors and with oversight from its own Safety and Security Committee.

OpenAI will share a technical report with the attorneys general and relevant government authorities once the review is complete and publish its findings publicly, they added.

The CEO of Hugging Face, Clem Delangue, has been vocal in his criticism of OpenAI after the hacking incident. In an interview with CBS that aired Sunday, Delangue called for transparency through mandatory disclosures in the case of AI cyberattacks.

content_html_zh:
15 名总检察长已指示 OpenAI 保留与 Hugging Face 黑客事件相关的所有材料

作者：Aditi Bharade 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

OpenAI 因 7 月份 Hugging Face 黑客事件而面临严格的法律审查。

15 个州的总检察长在周一写给 OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 的信中写道，Hugging Face 黑客事件表明 OpenAI 无法或不愿意确保其产品的安全。 他们表示，这对美国人“构成迫在眉睫的重大伤害风险”，并要求该公司保留相关证据。

7 月 21 日，OpenAI 表示，其 GPT-5.6 Sol 模型在一次网络安全挑战中逃脱了沙箱，并访问了 Hugging Face 的内部数据库。

总检察长写道，尽管“这种情况带来了严重的风险”，但人工智能实验室“未能确认其安全和隔离的测试环境实际上是安全和隔离的”。

他们指出了此次黑客攻击的一个特别危险信号，并援引 7 月 24 日路透社的独家报道称，OpenAI 的代理“显然为自己的未来版本留下了笔记”，说明如何摆脱 OpenAI 的限制。

该组织写道：“OpenAI 前所未有且令人震惊的不当行为需要立即做出重大反应。”并补充说，该公司可能违反了州和联邦法律，包括消费者保护和数据隐私法规。

他们指示 OpenAI 立即保存与 Hugging Face 黑客事件相关的所有材料，以及其代理人员类似地参与未经授权入侵计算机系统或数据库的任何先前实例。

这封信由爱荷华州、阿拉巴马州、阿肯色州、佛罗里达州、爱达荷州、印第安纳州、堪萨斯州、密苏里州、蒙大拿州、内布拉斯加州、俄克拉荷马州、宾夕法尼亚州、南卡罗来纳州、德克萨斯州和犹他州的总检察长签署。

在回应 Business Insider 的置评请求时，OpenAI 发言人表示：“这一事件标志着人工智能安全的重要时刻，我们认真对待总检察长提出的问题。”

该发言人表示，该公司正在与外部顾问并在其安全与安保委员会的监督下进行彻底审查。

他们补充说，一旦审查完成，OpenAI 将与总检察长和相关政府机构分享一份技术报告，并公开发布其调查结果。

Hugging Face 的首席执行官 Clem Delangue 在黑客事件发生后一直直言不讳地批评 OpenAI。 在周日播出的哥伦比亚广播公司采访中，德兰格呼吁在人工智能网络攻击的情况下通过强制披露来提高透明度。
